guideTitle: Best 3 in 1 Electric Window Vacuum Squeegees (2026)
metaTitle: Best 3 in 1 Electric Window Vacuum Squeegees
metaDescription: Six cordless window vacuum squeegees that spray, scrub and vacuum compared on blade width, battery runtime, tank size and poles for tall glass and showers.
expertTake: The Karcher WV 2 is the pick for most homes: a known brand, an angle-independent design that works sideways or upside down, and parts you can still buy in years. The SEESII is the value pick with two squeegee widths and a detachable battery rated for up to 60 minutes. If you only clean a few small windows a year, a plain squeegee and a microfiber cloth will do the job for far less.
introParagraphs: A window vacuum squeegee sprays or wipes on cleaner, then pulls the dirty water off the glass into a small onboard tank, so there are no drips down the wall and no streaks from a hand squeegee. The three jobs are spray, scrub and vacuum, and the machine does only the last one. Choose by the glass you clean most often, not the largest number on the box.

This guide explains what suction numbers mean on glass, how blade width and battery decide how many panes you clean per charge, and when an extension pole is worth having. Use the picks above as a shortlist, then read the reviews to match one of them to your windows, showers and mirrors.

products.name: Karcher WV 2 Universal Cordless Window Vacuum Squeegee

specList.label: Orientation
specList.value: Works at any angle, even upside down

products.description:
The Karcher WV 2 earns the top spot for its working design and its brand. The listing describes 360 degree comfort technology, which lets you clean sideways or completely upside down without the tank spilling into the nozzle. That matters on a shower door or a skylight, where most cheap models suck air and leave drips.

The built-in electric vacuum pulls dirty water away from the glass in one pass, and the same tool works on mirrors and glass shower enclosures. Compared with the WV 1 Plus, the WV 2 is the more flexible, cordless universal model. Both come from a company that sells pressure washers and cleaning gear and stocks spare blades and parts.

Keep the glass wet with cleaner, since a dry blade drags and skips. Replace the blade when it nicks and empty the tank after each session. Charge it fully and store it indoors, not in a cold garage where the battery loses capacity. Start each pane at the top corner, make a slow pass in an S-shaped path and finish at the bottom edge, where a dry cloth catches the last drops. Keep a second battery charged if the maker sells one, since a dead pack halfway through a house is the most common frustration.
products.bestFor: A household that cleans windows, mirrors and glass showers and wants a brand with parts support.
pros: Works at any angle including upside down
cons: Visible listing gives no battery capacity

products.name: Karcher WV 1 Plus Electric Window Vacuum 10 Inch
products.description:
The WV 1 Plus is the smaller Karcher: a 10 inch electric squeegee weighing 1.1 lb that sits comfortably in the hand. The listing says it cleans three times faster than a manual squeegee on windows, showers and mirrors and gives a simple routine: spray, wipe, vacuum. It also gives a pro tip for textured tile, where you apply pressure carefully.

Weight is the point. At 1.1 lb you can hold it overhead at a bathroom ceiling mirror or a high shower pane without tiring, which a heavier unit cannot do. The 10 inch blade is slightly narrower than the 11 inch blades of imports, so it needs more passes on a big window but fits small panes better.

As with all squeegees, keep the surface wet and the blade clean. Wipe the blade between panes, and empty the tank before it overflows into the motor intake. For a shower, wet the whole door first and work from the top down so the tank collects the runoff. A light wipe of the corner seals afterward stops water spots from forming on the metal frame.
products.bestFor: A bathroom and small-window cleaner who values low weight and a known brand.

products.name: SEESII Electric Window Vacuum Squeegee 11 and 6.7 Inch Blades
products.description:
SEESII includes two TPU squeegee heads, 11 inch for wide panes and 6.7 inch for small ones and tight corners, which is the most practical accessory set in the group. A detachable 2000 mAh lithium-ion battery is rated for up to 60 minutes of uniform suction, and the listing states 2000Pa maximum suction.

A detachable battery is a real ownership advantage, since a worn pack can be replaced instead of retiring the whole tool. The 2000Pa figure is a marketing number with no standard test; blade shape and flatness matter more. Compared with the Karcher WV 2, the SEESII gives you more accessories and runtime on paper but a less established brand.

Swap to the small blade for cabinet doors and shower corners, and keep the big blade for windows. Wipe both blades after use and store them dry. Swap blades by pulling the old one off the slot and clicking the new one on until it seats flat, and always check that no gap shows along the edge. Store the unused blade in a zip bag so dust does not dull it.
products.bestFor: Whole-house cleaning where two blade sizes and a swappable battery matter.
pros: TPU blades for glass and tile
cons: Suction figure has no standard test

products.name: Kiato Window Vacuum Squeegee 11 Inch with Spray Bottle 45 Minutes
products.description:
Kiato provides an 11 inch vacuum squeegee with a 2200 mAh battery, a stated 45 minute runtime, a modest 1.2 kPa suction claim and a 200 ml detachable tank. A spray bottle comes in the kit, so you can mix your own cleaner at the right strength.

The 1.2 kPa figure is lower than the 2000Pa claims of imports, though it is a more believable number. Detachable tanks are easier to empty and rinse than fixed ones, and 200 ml is on the larger side for the category. Compared with the SEESII, the Kiato has the bigger battery and tank but only one blade.

One bottle of cleaner goes further if you mist the glass lightly; a soaked pane overflows the tank quickly. Empty the tank every few panes and dry the blade between sessions. Fill the spray bottle with a few drops of dish soap and warm water, mist lightly and let the solution sit for a minute on greasy glass. Empty the tank into a sink, not onto the lawn, since cleaner can mark grass.
products.bestFor: Windows of moderate size where a bigger tank and a spray bottle simplify the routine.
cons: No extension pole in the listing

products.name: SOMZOKY 2000Pa Window Vacuum Squeegee with 31 to 40 Inch Pole
products.description:
SOMZOKY ships two identical 11 inch squeegee blades, one for daily use and one spare, plus a 31 to 40 inch stainless steel extension pole, a 2200 mAh battery and a 150 ml tank. A spare blade is genuinely useful, because a nicked blade leaves streaks and replacements are not always easy to find.

The extension pole lets you reach higher panes without a ladder, but poles add wobble. At 40 inches you work at arm's length, and the squeegee pressure is harder to control. Against the GARYOG, which offers the same pole range and the same battery, the SOMZOKY makes its spare blade the selling point.

Use the pole for the top row and your hand for the rest. Clean the blade after every pane, and rinse the tank with fresh water. Check the pole's locking collar before you climb, and never extend it near power lines. Use the pole only for the top row and switch to hand use for the rest.
products.bestFor: Windows with a high top row where a pole and a spare blade save a ladder.
cons: Pole adds wobble at full extension

products.badge: Best Runtime Claim for Pole Kit
products.name: GARYOG Electric Window Vacuum with 2 Squeegees and 31 to 40 Inch Pole
products.description:
GARYOG lists a 2200 mAh battery with up to 40 minutes of cleaning, 2000Pa suction and a 31 to 40 inch extendable pole, with two squeegees in the kit. The listing says a full charge provides about 35 minutes in one place and up to 40 in another, so treat the runtime as a range of 35 to 40.

It is nearly identical to the SOMZOKY on paper, which suggests both come from the same factory. That is not unusual in this category, and it means the choice comes down to price, the blade count and whichever listing has the better return policy. Compared with the Karcher models, it offers the pole and the kit at a lower cost but without a service network.

Check the pole joints for play when you receive it, tighten the locking collar and keep a spare blade ready. Charge fully before a big job. Look at the pole joints and the battery contacts when the kit arrives, and note the return window on the listing. A quick test on a small pane shows whether the blade seats flat.
products.bestFor: A buyer who wants the pole kit at a budget and accepts an unbranded tool.

buyingCriteria.explanation: You wet the glass with cleaner and scrub, then draw the vacuum blade across it. The blade scrapes the water into a slot and a fan pulls it into a small tank. It removes streaks and drips. The three jobs are spray, scrub and vacuum, and the tool only does the last. Count the panes in your home and multiply by two minutes to estimate the runtime you need.

SEESII, SOMZOKY and GARYOG state 2000Pa, while Kiato states a more modest 1.2 kPa. There is no standard test, so use the numbers only loosely. Blade flatness and glass wetness decide pickup more than the headline figure. A tool that handles odd angles is worth more than a higher suction claim.

Eleven inch blades cover a pane quickly. Smaller blades like the SEESII's 6.7 inch or the Karcher WV 1 Plus at 10 inches fit corners and small panes. A kit with two sizes covers both. A spare blade is cheap and prevents a day of streaks.

The SEESII claims up to 60 minutes, the Kiato about 45, and the GARYOG 35 to 40. A typical window takes a minute or two, so even 35 minutes covers a whole house. Detachable batteries extend the tool's life. Check whether the tank detaches, since a fixed tank is awkward to rinse.

Tanks hold 150 to 200 ml, and a large window fills one in a few passes. A detachable tank like the Kiato's is easier to empty. Overflowing a tank can spill into the motor. Think about how high your windows are before paying for a pole.

A 31 to 40 inch pole on the SOMZOKY and GARYOG reaches high panes. It also adds wobble and reduces pressure control. Use it only for the top row. Test on a small pane first to learn how much cleaner you need.

howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each tool handles awkward angles. The Karcher WV 2's any-angle design stood out. Angle-independent design counted for real glass.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade and kit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared blade sizes and spares. SEESII and SOMZOKY offer the most useful sets, based on the spec sheet. Spare blades and sizes counted as value.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We read stated runtimes. The SEESII's up to 60 minutes leads, with the others near 35 to 45. Stated minutes were compared directly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tank and reach
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank sizes and poles. The Kiato's 200 ml tank and the pole kits stood out. Detachable tanks counted as a plus.

howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed brand history and price tier, judged against owner feedback patterns. We evaluated every pick against the same checklist. Spare parts availability counted for more than marketing.

cards.label: Branded
cards.text: The Karcher WV 2 and WV 1 Plus come with a service network and spare parts. They cost more.

cards.label: Import
cards.text: The SEESII, Kiato, SOMZOKY and GARYOG offer kits and poles for less. They are similar to each other and have thin support.

howToChoose.note: Choose branded for long-term use, import for a low-cost kit. Either way, keep a spare blade in the kit.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A small, light blade that works sideways and upside down and a tank that does not spill at an angle. Textured tile needs care.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Karcher WV 2 and WV 1 Plus fit best, and the SEESII's small blade helps in corners.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You clean often and want durable parts. The Karcher WV 2 earns it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clean a few windows a year. A GARYOG or Kiato covers it.

maintenance.why: Grit on the blade scratches and streaks glass. A quick wipe keeps it clean. A damp cloth is enough.
Standing dirty water smells and grows mold. Rinse and air dry it. Dry it before storage.
A damaged edge leaves streaks. Spare blades cost little. Keep a spare in a bag.
Avoid cold garages and overnight charging on soft surfaces. Store it indoors.
Locking collars loosen and cause wobble. Tighten them before climbing. A drop of lubricant helps the joints.

faq.q: Does a window vacuum replace a squeegee?
faq.a: It does the same job with less dripping. You still spray and scrub. A hand squeegee is cheaper, but the vacuum saves wall mess and time. Mist the glass lightly and work from the top down.
Poorly. Textured or etched glass traps water and can drag the blade. Apply light pressure or use a cloth. A quick test on a small corner shows whether the blade skips.
With 35 to 60 minutes claimed, a whole house is possible. A typical pane takes a minute or two. Larger panes take longer. Plan a session by room and recharge between floors if your home is large.
Only for high panes. Poles add wobble. A hand-held tool is easier on ordinary windows and showers. A lightweight hand-held tool is safer than a long pole on a wet ladder.
A mild glass cleaner or diluted dish soap. Strong ammonia can degrade seals. Mist rather than soak. Rinse the tank after every use to keep odors away.
A dirty or nicked blade, a dry pane or a full tank. Wipe the blade, wet the glass and empty the tank. Replace the blade at the first sign of streaking.
